title: Before trusting an in-memory cache (e.g. a property set on the `store` object) to save work across h
body:
Before trusting an in-memory cache (e.g. a property set on the `store` object) to save work across hook invocations, check whether the code path is reached only through an ephemeral per-event process (PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop via run.js) or through a long-lived process (the MCP server in src/mcp/server.js, or the audit UI). A cache written on `store` only pays off in the long-lived case; in the ephemeral case a fresh store is constructed every hook event, so the cache always misses and the guarded work (stat/readdir/readFile, hashing, etc.) still runs every time. Concretely: `projectContext()` in src/engine/project-context.js sets `store.projectContextCache` (lines 23, 54), but every PreToolUse call reopens a new store in a new Node process, so it never hits outside the MCP/UI process — every tool call still pays 6 stat() + 1 readdir() + up to 5 readFile() calls. If a cache needs to survive across ephemeral hook processes, it has to be persisted in the SQLite derived index (already the pattern used by loadConfig), not just kept as a JS object property.

Why: L1 in docs/architecture/plugin-constraints.md states one Node process is spawned per hook event and explicitly forbids 'amortising a cost after the first call' because there is no second call in the same process. Reading src/engine/project-context.js and src/hooks/run.js together shows an in-memory cache that silently violates this: it looks like an optimization but only ever activates in the two processes (MCP server, audit UI) that persist, not in the default single-developer path with no UI/MCP server running.

evidence.summary: projectContextCache is a plain property on the store object, set/read at lines 23 and 54, with no persistence layer.
L1 states hooks are ephemeral Node processes, one per event, and forbids amortizing cost after the first call since there is no second call in the same process.
openStore is called fresh inside each hook invocation for the non-bridged path, so any per-store in-memory cache is discarded when the process exits.

v1.trigger: Reviewing or optimizing PreToolUse/observe/prompt hook cost, or adding an in-memory cache on the store object anywhere in src/engine or src/hooks.
